title: Easy Vegan Chickpea Curry
description: A creamy coconut and tomato curry that comes together in one pot.
intro: This easy vegan chickpea curry is creamy, gently spiced and made from pantry staples in 35 minutes. It's naturally gluten-free and dairy-free, and it tastes even better the next day.

image.alt: Easy vegan chickpea curry in a white bowl with basmati rice, spinach and fresh coriander

ingredients.item: Fresh coriander and cooked rice, to serve

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, until soft and golden.
steps.tip: Don't rush the onions — gentle cooking builds most of the flavour.
steps.timer_done: The onion should be soft and golden. If not, give it a few more minutes.

steps.text: Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
steps.timer_done: Fragrant? Move straight on so the garlic doesn't burn.

steps.text: Stir in the curry powder, cumin and turmeric and toast for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and simmer until slightly thickened.
steps.timer_done: The tomatoes should look slightly thicker, then move on.

steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk, add the chickpeas and simmer uncovered, stirring now and then.
steps.timer_done: Check the sauce has thickened, then move on.

steps.text: Stir in the spinach until just wilted, about 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat, add the lime juice and season with salt.
steps.tip: Taste and adjust — a little more lime or salt makes a big difference.

steps.text: Serve over rice, topped with fresh coriander.

article_html:
A weeknight curry from the pantry

This is the curry we make when the fridge looks empty. Onions, a few spices, a can of tomatoes, coconut milk and chickpeas simmer into something rich and comforting, with spinach and lime stirred in at the end for freshness.

Why you'll love this recipe

  • One pot, 35 minutes, start to finish.
  • Made from pantry staples you probably already have.
  • Naturally vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free — no swaps needed.
  • Freezes well, so it's ideal for batch cooking.

Ingredients overview

  • Chickpeas: Canned keeps it quick. Rinse well for a cleaner flavour.
  • Coconut milk: Full-fat gives the creamiest sauce; light works but is thinner.
  • Curry powder: Mild or medium. Some blends contain wheat flour, so check the label says gluten-free.
  • Spinach & lime: Added at the end, so the spinach stays bright and the lime lifts the whole pot.

Substitutions and variations

  • No coconut milk? Stir in 200 g unsweetened soy yogurt off the heat.
  • Kale instead of spinach: Add it 3 minutes earlier so it softens.
  • Heartier: Add 1 diced sweet potato with the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes longer.
  • More heat: Cook 1 chopped green chili with the garlic.
  • Dried chickpeas: Use 250 g, soaked overnight and cooked until tender.

Step-by-step instructions

1. Build the base

Cook the onion slowly with a pinch of salt until soft and golden — about 8 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, then toast the spices for just 30 seconds.

2. Simmer

Tomatoes go in first to cook down, then coconut milk and chickpeas. Leave it uncovered for 15 minutes so the sauce thickens.

3. Finish and taste

Wilt in the spinach, take the pan off the heat and add lime and salt. Taste, adjust, and let it rest for a few minutes.

Tips for success

  • Don't rush the onions — gentle cooking builds most of the flavour.
  • Spices burn quickly; 30 seconds in the pan is enough.
  • The curry thickens as it stands, so loosen leftovers with a splash of water.

storage.fridge: Up to 4 days in an airtight container.
storage.freezer: Up to 3 months, without rice. Thaw overnight in the fridge.
storage.reheat: Gently on the stove with a splash of water until piping hot.
storage.summary: Leftovers keep for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

faq.question: Is chickpea curry healthy?
faq.answer: It's built on whole foods — chickpeas, tomatoes, spinach and spices — and is filling thanks to the fibre and plant protein in the chickpeas. Use light coconut milk for a lighter sauce.

faq.question: Is this curry spicy?
faq.answer: It's mild as written. Add a green chili with the garlic or use a hot curry powder for more heat.

faq.question: Is curry powder gluten-free?
faq.answer: Most pure spice blends are, but some add wheat flour. Choose one labelled gluten-free.

faq.question: Can I freeze chickpea curry?
faq.answer: Yes, for up to 3 months. Freeze it without rice and thaw overnight in the fridge.

faq.question: What do you serve with chickpea curry?
faq.answer: Basmati rice, quinoa or warm gluten-free flatbread all work well.

title: Gluten-Free Banana Oat Pancakes
description: Fluffy, naturally sweet pancakes made with certified gluten-free oats.
intro: These gluten-free banana oat pancakes are blended in one jug and ready in 20 minutes. Ripe bananas sweeten them, so they need no added sugar.

image.alt: Stack of gluten-free banana oat pancakes with sliced banana and maple syrup

ingredients.item: Berries and maple syrup, to serve

steps.text: Blend the bananas, oats, eggs, milk, baking powder, cinnamon and salt until smooth.
Let the batter rest so the oats thicken it slightly.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and add a little butter.
Pour in 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake and cook until bubbles appear on top.
Flip and cook the other side until golden.
Serve warm with berries and maple syrup.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Use very ripe, spotty bananas for the sweetest pancakes.
  • Keep the heat at medium — oat batter browns faster than wheat batter.

storage.fridge: Up to 2 days, layered with baking paper.
storage.reheat: In a toaster or dry pan until warmed through.

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl
description: Lemony quinoa, crisp vegetables, chickpeas and crumbled feta.
intro: This Mediterranean quinoa bowl packs crunchy vegetables, chickpeas and feta into a bright lemon-herb dressing. It's ready in 25 minutes and keeps well for packed lunches.

image.alt: Mediterranean quinoa bowl with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, olives, chickpeas and feta

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in the water, covered, until the water is absorbed.
Take off the heat, leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic, salt and pepper.
Toss the quinoa with half the dressing.
Divide into bowls and top with chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion and olives.
Finish with feta, parsley and the rest of the dressing.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Rinse quinoa well to remove its bitter coating.
  • Keep the dressing separate if packing for lunch.

title: Fudgy Gluten-Free Brownies
description: Rich, chewy brownies made with almond flour instead of wheat.
intro: These fudgy gluten-free brownies use almond flour for a rich, chewy middle and a crackly top. Nobody will guess they're gluten-free.

image.alt: Fudgy gluten-free brownies cut into squares on baking paper

steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter and chocolate together over low heat, then cool slightly.
Whisk in the sugar, then the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, until glossy.
Fold in the almond flour, cocoa and salt until just combined.
Spread into the tin and bake until the edges are set but the centre is still soft.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 16 squares.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Don't overbake: a slightly wobbly centre means a fudgy brownie.
  • Chill before cutting for clean edges.

storage.fridge: Up to 5 days in an airtight box.

title: Vegan Red Lentil Soup
description: A warming, cumin-spiced soup finished with a squeeze of lemon.
intro: This vegan red lentil soup is thick, warming and made in one pot in 40 minutes. Cumin and smoked paprika give it depth, and lemon keeps it bright.

image.alt: Bowl of vegan red lentil soup with a lemon wedge and olive oil drizzle

steps.text: Heat the oil and soften the onion and carrots.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the lentils, tomatoes and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer until the lentils collapse.
Blend about half the soup for a creamy texture with some body.
Season with lemon juice and salt and serve.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.
  • Thin with extra stock if reheating — it thickens as it stands.

storage.reheat: On the stove, adding a splash of water.

title: Roasted Vegetable Salad with Tahini
description: Caramelised squash, cauliflower and chickpeas with a lemony tahini drizzle.
intro: This roasted vegetable salad turns squash, cauliflower and chickpeas into a filling dinner. A lemony tahini dressing ties it together.

image.alt: Roasted butternut squash, cauliflower and chickpeas over greens with tahini drizzle

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss the squash, cauliflower, chickpeas and onion with the oil, spices and salt on a large tray.
Roast, turning halfway, until golden at the edges.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup and water into a pourable dressing.
Toss the warm vegetables with the greens, drizzle with dressing and scatter over the pumpkin seeds.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Spread the vegetables out — crowded trays steam instead of roast.
  • Dry the chickpeas well so they crisp.

storage.fridge: Roasted vegetables keep 3 days; add greens and dressing when serving.

title: Overnight Oats with Berries
description: Five minutes of prep tonight, a ready breakfast tomorrow.
intro: These overnight oats with berries take ten minutes to stir together and are ready when you wake up. They're vegan, and gluten-free when made with certified gluten-free oats.

image.alt: Two jars of overnight oats topped with fresh berries

steps.text: Stir the oats, almond milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup and vanilla together.
Divide between two jars, cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 6 hours.
Loosen with a splash of milk if needed and top with berries.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Make 3 days' worth at once — they keep well.

storage.fridge: Up to 3 days, berries added on the day.

title: High-Protein Crispy Tofu Bowl
description: Golden tofu, brown rice, edamame and a ginger-sesame sauce.
intro: This high-protein crispy tofu bowl stacks golden tofu, edamame and brown rice with a punchy ginger-sesame sauce. It's a 30-minute dinner that keeps you full.

image.alt: Crispy tofu cubes over brown rice with edamame, carrot and cucumber

ingredients.item: Sesame seeds and spring onion, to serve

steps.text: Press the tofu between kitchen towels under a heavy pan.
Cut into cubes and toss with the cornflour.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat, turning, until crisp on all sides.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, maple syrup and ginger.
Cook the edamame in boiling water.
Build bowls with rice, tofu, edamame, carrot and cucumber, then spoon over the sauce and finish with sesame and spring onion.

article_html:
Tips for success

  • Pressing the tofu is what makes it crisp — don't skip it.

storage.fridge: Up to 3 days; tofu softens but stays tasty.

title: Healthy Avocado Toast
description: Creamy avocado, chili flakes and lime on toasted sourdough.
intro: This healthy avocado toast with chili and lime takes 10 minutes and beats any café version. Use gluten-free bread to make it gluten-free.

image.alt: Avocado toast with chili flakes, lime and coriander on sourdough

steps.text: Toast the bread until golden.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice, salt and pepper.
Spread over the toast and finish with chili flakes, olive oil and coriander.

title: Peanut Butter Energy Bites
description: No-bake bites with oats, peanut butter, dates and maple syrup.
intro: These peanut butter energy bites are a no-bake snack you can make in 15 minutes. They're vegan, and gluten-free with certified gluten-free oats.

image.alt: Peanut butter energy bites on a plate with a few chocolate chips

steps.text: Blitz the dates in a food processor until they form a paste.
Add the oats, peanut butter, maple syrup, flaxseed and salt and pulse until it holds together.
Stir in the chocolate chips and roll into 16 balls.
Chill to firm up before eating.
